sources.source_hash_scope: Saved UTF-8 text excerpt from the web PDF reader; not the original PDF bytes
sources.retrieval_note: The web PDF reader exposed the relevant pages; direct fetch from the local retrieval environment returned HTTP 404, so the original PDF-byte hash is unavailable.
sources.note: The deck states that B747/B767/B777/B787 airframe-maintenance counts lead globally and that A350/B737MAX capabilities and customer expansion are under development. It separately says 30 global major customers and eighth place in overall global airframe maintenance capacity; these are different metrics from airline count and B747-specific heavy-check ranking.

sources.title: In Photos: Inside the EGAT facilities in Taipei - Airways
sources.note: Airways attributes to Cirium the finding that EGAT is the world's largest provider of C/heavy checks on four-engine aircraft; it says the work is exclusively Boeing 747 and calls EGAT the largest 747 MRO provider worldwide. It reports more than 1,000 747 heavy-check events, compared with 845 on 767 and 750 on 777.

retrieval_observations.observed_result: Official-host web open returned 403; local direct fetch returned 404
retrieval_observations.semantic_consequence: Not relied upon. The current EGAT company page independently states more than 40 airlines; the annual-report search excerpt was treated only as a discovery lead.

search_notes: The 2025 deck's 30 global major customers is not treated as a contradiction of the company page's more-than-40 airline figure because the wording and denominator differ.
The deck's eighth-place ranking is overall airframe-maintenance capacity; the B747 ranking is a narrower heavy-check/MRO claim sourced to the Cirium-referencing industry article.
